answer: Admission runs through one narrow inlet: a new agent is seated only after it gathers a vouch-quorum from established peers, and each voucher's signing weight decays quadratically with every identity it has already backed this window, while co-signers post a bond slashed if their pick is later caught colluding. A farm of k clones cannot cheaply self-admit, since spending its own seats' thinning vouch-budget forfeits weight and risks those bonds, and honest strangers will not vouch for free. Real standing accrues glacier-slow; the trust graph branches like a pruned vine, not a thicket.
